R1: an entry must name its format — null, undefined, a non-object, a missing, empty or non-string format all throw
R10: pass 1 asks every entry detect(bytes, null) in registration order and returns the first truthy result carrying .format, verbatim
R11: pass 2 runs only when pass 1 had no hit and a content type is provided; asks detect(null, contentType) in order; first hit verbatim
R12, R17: the reasons the registry states are read by their word keys
R12: no hit in either pass returns the stated undetermined with both reasons
R13: the only answers are an entry's verbatim result or the stated undetermined; an entry's detect error propagates
R2: detect must be a function
R24: one entry per format key, and registration order is the order listFormats and both detect passes iterate
R25: detectFormat's answer for one registry state and one pair of inputs never changes; nothing here reads the clock or the network
R26: bytes always outrank a declared content type — every entry has pass 1 before any entry sees pass 2
R27: an unmatched input is a stated undetermined with why; an unknown key is null from getFormat and unregisterFormat, never a throw
R3: parts, structure and text are each optional; present and not a function throws naming the slot
R4: a second registration under a held format throws, and the existing entry stays in place
R5: the entry is stored and returned unchanged — not cloned, no default filled — and reachable from getFormat and detectFormat
R6: unregisterFormat removes and returns the entry; an unknown key answers null, changes nothing, never throws
R7: getFormat returns the stored entry exactly as received, or null; never throws
R8: listFormats returns every key in registration order; a re-registered format moves to the end
R9: bytes count only as a non-empty Uint8Array; a content type only as a non-empty string
